title: What is TSMC?
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) is the world's largest semiconductor manufacturer, producing chips for major tech companies like Apple, Amazon, and Google. It focuses solely on manufacturing for third parties, unlike competitors, and boasts significant market dominance and advanced process technology. The article also discusses the potential impact of a Chinese invasion of Taiwan on TSMC and its global operations, as well as the company's expansion plans in the US.

title: Apple’s market value drops below $2 trillion
summary: Apple Inc.'s market capitalization fell below $2 trillion for the first time since March 2021, driven by concerns over high inflation and a slowing global economy impacting demand for its products. This significant drop follows a year after the company briefly reached a $3 trillion valuation. Analysts have downgraded Apple due to anticipated supply chain issues and reduced consumer spending on high-end phones, forecasting a potential revenue decline.

title: Amazon's AWS Growth Strategy Probably More Sustainable Than Oracle's (AMZN)
summary: The article compares the sustainability of growth strategies between Amazon's AWS and Oracle. While Oracle has seen growth due to acquisitions and price cutting, AWS's growth is attributed to its vertically integrated cloud infrastructure and product strength, accounting for a significant portion of Amazon's profits. The author suggests Oracle's strategy may not be sustainable given its debt-to-sales ratio and profitability, and advises that Oracle needs a clearer plan for profitable growth.

title: First Trust Dow Jones Internet Index Fund (FDN) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the First Trust Dow Jones Internet Index Fund (FDN), including its stock price, key statistics, top holdings, and performance. The article also presents financial ranks, dividend data, and historical performance charts for FDN.

title: Amazon to slash more than 18,000 jobs in an escalation of cuts
summary: Amazon is laying off over 18,000 employees, a significant increase from its previously announced cuts, as the technology sector experiences a deepening slump. The reductions are primarily within Amazon's corporate retail division and human resources, reflecting a shift to a stronger cost structure amid uncertain economic conditions. This move follows similar workforce reductions by other tech giants like Salesforce, and investors reacted positively to Amazon's decision.

title: Salesforce to cut 10% of workforce in latest tech layoffs
summary: Salesforce Inc. announced it will cut 10% of its workforce and close some offices, aiming to reduce costs after rapid hiring during the pandemic. Co-CEO Marc Benioff stated the company hired "too many people" leading into the current economic downturn, taking responsibility for the over-hiring. This move follows similar workforce reductions by other tech giants like Meta and Amazon, as companies prepare for a potential deep downturn amid rising interest rates and a challenging economic environment.

title: Distributed Cloud Global Market Report 2022: Ukraine-Russia War Impact
summary: The global distributed cloud market is projected to grow significantly, from $2.84 billion in 2021 to $7.42 billion in 2026, despite disruptions caused by the Russia-Ukraine war and the COVID-19 pandemic. This growth is driven by the increasing adoption of distributed cloud architectures to meet performance, compliance, and edge computing demands. Technological innovation, such as F5's Distributed Cloud WAAP, is a key trend, with companies focusing on advanced solutions to secure and manage applications across multi-cloud environments.

title: News | Industrial Project Completions and Easing Demand Drive Up Vacancy Rate
summary: The industrial real estate market is facing an increase in vacancy rates due to a wave of new industrial project completions initiated during the pandemic and easing demand in a slowing economy. CBRE forecasts a significant decline in leasing activity, though 2023 is still expected to be a strong year. Despite current inventory, new warehouse construction starts are projected to hit a seven-year low, potentially leading to a shortage in 2024.

title: Private Wireless Partnership Part of the Perks at JBG SMITH’s National Landing
summary: JBG SMITH and Federated Wireless have partnered to create the nation's first converged digital infrastructure platform at National Landing in Northern Virginia. This initiative provides tenants and residents with robust and customizable private 5G networks, addressing the increasing demand for high-speed connectivity and advanced digital services in commercial real estate. This strategic investment in digital infrastructure enhances property value and tenant retention in a competitive market.

title: 2023 brings more jobs cuts for Mass. tech workers
summary: Cambridge-based Pegasystems announced a 4% workforce reduction, while San Francisco-based Salesforce, with significant Massachusetts operations, stated it would cut 10% of its employees. Both software companies, which saw increased sales during the pandemic, attribute these job cuts to over-hiring during that period and the current economic slowdown. These layoffs follow similar trends in the tech industry from the previous year.

title: Salesforce to lay off 10% of workforce to cut costs amid economic downturn
summary: Salesforce announced it will lay off 10% of its workforce and reduce office space to cut operating costs amid a challenging economic environment. CEO Marc Benioff admitted the company "hired too many people" during the pandemic's revenue surge, and the company is now facing the consequences. This move follows similar cost-cutting measures by other tech giants like Amazon, Apple, and Meta Platforms.

title: Lionsgate International SVP Marc Lorber To Exit
summary: Marc Lorber, Lionsgate's SVP of International TV Co-Productions and Acquisitions, is leaving the studio after nearly a decade. Lorber, who joined in 2013, was instrumental in identifying and co-developing scripted TV dramas, miniseries, and comedies globally, working on projects like "Motherland" and "The Pact." His departure coincides with significant shifts at Lionsgate, including the spin-off of its studio from Starz and alterations to its streaming services.

title: Cisco Systems to eliminate 80 jobs in San Francisco
summary: Cisco Systems is eliminating 80 jobs in San Francisco as part of global job losses announced in November. This information was detailed in letters sent to California employment officials by the company. The layoffs affect the San Francisco office, while the company's headquarters remain in San Jose.

title: Opinion: Amazon cuts jobs to reset tech giant after monster growth in the pandemic, but investors still worried
summary: Amazon has announced significant job cuts, totaling 18,000 positions, which is seen as a move to reset the company after rapid pandemic-era growth. While analysts view these cost-cutting measures positively, investors remain concerned, particularly due to a slowdown in Amazon's highly profitable AWS cloud business. This situation has led to investor jitters despite the company's efforts to streamline operations.

title: Apple brings AI narration to audiobooks
summary: Apple Inc. has introduced AI-narrated audiobooks through Apple Books, utilizing text-to-speech technology to make audiobook production more accessible and affordable for publishers and authors. While the digital voices aim to reduce costs and complexity, some critics note an "artificial edge" compared to human narrators. Apple plans to improve the AI voices and currently offers them for select English-language romance and fiction books, with more voices and nonfiction categories in development.

title: Opendoor: The Future 'Amazon Of Real Estate' At A Compelling Valuation
summary: Opendoor's stock, like many SPACs, has plummeted, trading significantly below its original SPAC price and previous highs. Despite outperforming initial SPAC estimates before this year, the company now faces heightened risks due to the challenging macro environment and rising interest rates impacting the real estate market. However, with its new third-party Marketplace offering in select cities, Opendoor still possesses a substantial long-term growth opportunity, with current investor sentiment potentially offering a compelling valuation.

title: PurpleUrchin Bypasses CAPTCHA and Steals Cloud Platform Resources
summary: Unit 42 researchers at Palo Alto Networks have identified a "freejacking" campaign called PurpleUrchin, orchestrated by the threat actor group Automated Libra. This group exploits free or limited-time cloud resources, leveraging DevOps automation and CAPTCHA bypass techniques to conduct cryptocurrency mining operations. They also employ a "Play and Run" tactic, creating fake accounts with fraudulent credit card information to incur unpaid balances on cloud service platforms, having created over 130,000 such accounts.

title: Amazon to cut 18,000 jobs as layoffs expand in tech sector
summary: Amazon is cutting over 18,000 jobs, more than initially planned, affecting primarily its e-commerce and human resources divisions. CEO Andy Jassy cited the uncertain economy and rapid hiring as reasons for the significant workforce reduction, which follows similar layoffs in the tech sector. This move highlights a shift for Amazon from a pandemic-fueled growth period to a more cautious outlook.

title: Software company Pegasystems to lay off 4% workforce amid recession fears
summary: Software company Pegasystems is set to lay off 4% of its workforce, totaling over 6,000 employees, due to looming recession fears in 2023. This move is part of the company's strategy to improve its go-to-market operating model and is expected to incur a charge of $18.9 million in Q4 2022 for severance and benefit costs. Pegasystems joins other major tech firms like Amazon and Salesforce in announcing significant job cuts amid economic uncertainties.

title: The Dream of Portland Is Alive in Japan
summary: Japan has developed a strong infatuation with Portland, Oregon, viewing it as an aspirational brand representing a relaxed, creative, and nature-connected lifestyle. This fascination has led to Portland-themed establishments in Tokyo, a boom in Japanese tourism to Portland, and even investments in urban planning inspired by Portland's ethos. The phenomenon is driven by a desire for an alternative to the corporate grind and a cultural shift in Japan valuing community and slower living, though some believe this idealized view may be transient.

summary: This article reveals eight insider secrets for shopping on QVC, according to retail experts. The piece also delves into QVC's strategic marketing, focusing on generic products for a broad demographic, discounts on "as-is" items, and the psychological influence of its hosts, while cautioning against impulse purchases, especially on April Fool's Day.

title: You might actually want a TiVo TV someday
summary: Xperi, the company that owns the TiVo brand, is launching its own TiVo OS smart TV platform in Europe in the first half of 2023, with U.S. availability planned for the future. The platform focuses on content discovery over apps, offering recommendations across various streaming services and an intuitive voice search. While it currently lacks a robust app store compared to competitors, its neutral approach and potential for ad revenue sharing aim to attract TV manufacturers.

title: CVS eyes next-generation health clinics after Amazon’s move for One Medical
summary: CVS Health Corp. is expanding its healthcare services by investing $100 million in Carbon Health Inc., a chain of urgent- and primary-care clinics. Additionally, CVS is reportedly in negotiations to acquire Oak Street Health Inc., a chain specializing in Medicare recipients, for over $10 billion. These moves signal CVS's strategy to evolve from a drugstore chain into a full-service healthcare company in response to trends like Amazon's acquisition of One Medical.

title: Hot warehouse market shows signs of cooldown
summary: The demand for warehouse space continued to decline in Q4, with occupied space dropping 9.4% and vacancy rates reaching 3.3%. This slowdown is attributed to businesses reducing capital expansion amid inflationary pressures and economic uncertainty, even as more new warehouses are completed. Despite increased supply, rent growth has slowed significantly, offering potential benefits for businesses seeking new facilities and better amenities.

title: 10 Data Center Companies You Need To Watch In 2023
summary: The data center market is experiencing significant growth driven by digital transformation, IoT, 5G, and streaming content, with hyperscalers accounting for a large portion of this expansion. This article highlights ten key data center companies—including major players like AWS and Equinix, and rapidly growing firms like Aligned Data Centers and Evocative—that are making significant investments in new construction, acquisitions, and technological advancements to meet the escalating global demand for capacity and enhance their service offerings. These companies are adapting to market changes, such as leadership transitions and strategic partnerships, to expand their footprints and provide advanced infrastructure solutions worldwide.

title: Kroger launches health marketing campaign
summary: Kroger Health has initiated a new marketing campaign called “A World of Care Is In-Store” to promote its healthcare services, utilizing streaming video, radio, social media, and in-store signage. This move aims to compete with rivals like CVS Health and Walgreens by leveraging Kroger's extensive pharmacy and clinic network, and its significant presence in the US grocery market. The campaign highlights the synergy between in-store healthcare and healthy food programs, especially given Kroger's pending acquisition of Albertsons, which will expand its retail media network capabilities.

title: Amazon Expands Prime Delivery Service to More Web Stores
summary: Amazon is broadening its "Buy With Prime" program, allowing Prime subscribers to utilize the company's fast delivery services on participating third-party websites. Initially launched via invitation, the service will be widely accessible across the US by the end of January. Amazon reports that the program has significantly boosted conversions, with a 25% increase in purchases on sites integrating the service.

title: Helping Construction Firms Gain Useful Insights from Their Data
summary: Autodesk and Amazon have partnered to help construction firms leverage their abundant but often unused data. They are integrating Autodesk Construction Cloud with Amazon S3 and Redshift, allowing construction teams to synchronize project data and use advanced Amazon analytics, AI, and Machine Learning tools like Amazon Rekognition, Amazon Forecast, and Amazon QuickSight to gain actionable insights, improve efficiency, and enhance safety on job sites. This collaboration aims to make data analysis more accessible and powerful for construction professionals.

title: Stocks waver as traders eye US inflation and interest rates
summary: Global stock markets experienced fluctuations following a pessimistic economic forecast from the World Bank. Investors are awaiting critical inflation data and corporate earnings reports, with a particular focus on the upcoming US consumer price index. The Federal Reserve's future policy decisions regarding interest rate hikes to combat inflation remain a key concern, though some officials express hope for a "soft landing" despite the ongoing need for restrictive monetary policy.

title: Ramstad: A Minnesota company lost $1B in value as investors fled tech. Here's what it did next.
summary: Sezzle, a Minneapolis-based financial tech company, saw its market value plummet by 96% from its peak of over $1 billion in February 2021 as investors exited the tech sector. Despite significant layoffs and office closures, CEO Charlie Youakim pivoted the company's strategy towards profitability, leading to their first monthly profit in November and projected full-year profit for 2023. Sezzle's buy-now-pay-later platform is now used by 400,000 retailers and facilitates over $100 million in annual revenue.

title: Will Best Buy customers be okay with its rewards program changes?
summary: Best Buy is changing its "My Best Buy" rewards program, offering free standard shipping to all members but eliminating reward points for purchases unless customers use the Best Buy credit card. This move, seen as a response to Amazon Prime and Walmart+, comes as Best Buy faces declining same-store sales and aims to drive credit card usage while its Totaltech subscription plan has not met membership expectations. Retail experts and commenters express mixed reactions, with many questioning if the changes will alienate customers and genuinely boost sales or loyalty.

title: Amazon workers' union victory upheld by U.S. labor board director
summary: A U.S. labor board director has upheld the Amazon workers' union victory at a Staten Island warehouse, moving the company closer to bargaining with staff. Amazon plans to appeal the decision, arguing the election process was unfair. This landmark unionization marks the first time U.S. Amazon staff have unionized and is a significant moment for organized labor amid Amazon's recent layoffs and criticisms of its employee practices.

title: Skagen Falster Gen 6's long-awaited Wear OS 3 update is here
summary: The Skagen Falster Gen 6 smartwatch is finally receiving its Wear OS 3 update, following Fossil's Gen 6 series which updated in October 2022. This update brings a stock Wear OS experience, pre-installed apps like Alexa and Spotify, but notably still lacks Google Assistant, which remains exclusive to Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch models. Users should be aware that the update will factory reset their device, requiring a fresh setup via the Skagen Smartwatches app.

title: Amazon Fashion Launches Collaboration With Rent the Runway
summary: Amazon Fashion is launching an online storefront with Rent the Runway, expanding the rental company's reach beyond its subscription model. The collaboration will feature both previously worn and new designer styles, and Rent the Runway recognized approximately $4.6 million in revenue from this partnership in the quarter ending October 31st. This move aims to boost Amazon's existing apparel resale offerings.

title: Macy's CEO is 'cautious' about consumer spending after seeing dip in self purchases
summary: Macy's CEO Jeff Gennette expressed caution about consumer spending despite a strong holiday season, specifically noting a decline in "self purchases" during the lull periods in November and December. He also pointed to rising credit card balances and delinquencies among Macy's customers as signs of consumer pressure due to stubbornly high inflation. While acknowledging the strength of luxury brands like Bluemercury and Bloomingdale's, Gennette emphasized a need to be cautious but ready for market opportunities.

title: From Apple To Amazon And Toyota, Here Are The Top 10 Biggest Companies In The World
summary: This article lists the top 10 biggest companies in the world based on revenue. Walmart, State Grid Corporation Of China, and Amazon lead the list, primarily highlighting a competition between US and Chinese firms. The article also includes companies from Japan and Germany, detailing their revenue, founding year, and number of employees.

title: Ryder layoffs: 800 jobs to be cut at Applied Materials site
summary: Ryder System Inc. will cut 800 jobs and close its operations at the Applied Materials site in Austin, as disclosed in a letter to the Texas Workforce Commission. The transportation and logistics company expects "one or more other operators" to take over its responsibilities. This move comes despite Ryder reporting significant revenue increases in Q3 2022.

title: SoundHound axes nearly 50% of staff less than a year after IPO
summary: SoundHound, a speech and music recognition company, laid off nearly half of its remaining staff less than a year after its IPO. The company cited changing economic conditions and continued to book losses in Q3 2022 despite increased revenue. This move follows an earlier 10% staff reduction and comes amid widespread job cuts in the tech industry.

title: How Kroger, Whole Foods are upgrading labor management
summary: Kroger and Whole Foods are enhancing their labor management strategies by focusing on employee well-being, professional development, and efficient training. Whole Foods is reinventing its orientation and launching specialized training programs like the cake decorator apprenticeship, while Kroger is leveraging technology for rapid, scalable training and offering comprehensive well-being support to its vast workforce. Both retailers emphasize listening to employee feedback to create more fulfilling and supportive work environments.

title: Netflix set for slowest revenue growth as ad plan struggles to gain traction
summary: Netflix is projected to report its slowest quarterly revenue growth in the upcoming earnings report, largely due to its ad-supported plan failing to significantly attract new customers in the saturated U.S. market. Analysts suggest this lack of traction, coupled with rising costs and increased competition, could force the company to curb its content spending. Despite a return to subscriber growth in Q3 2022, the ad-supported tier's pricing and limited content are seen as deterrents for substantial growth.

title: Costco Wholesale Corp. stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) shares rose 0.31% on Tuesday, closing at $486.77, despite a general market decline for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The stock outperformed competitors like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) and Walmart Inc. (WMT), which both saw declines. Costco's trading volume was below its 50-day average.

title: 40-acre data center planned for former Westside Atlanta rail yard
summary: Endeavour is planning a 40-acre sustainable data center at Tilford Yard on Atlanta's Westside, a site that has previously attracted an Amazon facility. This development signifies continued growth in the area, following earlier sales of the CSX rail yard and plans for an Amazon delivery station.

title: Microsoft to shed 10,000 jobs, adding to glut of tech layoffs
summary: Microsoft announced it would eliminate 10,000 jobs and take a $1.2 billion charge to earnings as cloud-computing customers reduce spending and the company prepares for a potential recession. Despite this, Microsoft plans to increase investment in generative artificial intelligence, seen as a new growth area. The layoffs, affecting less than 5% of its workforce, are expected to conclude by the end of March, though strategic hiring will continue.

title: GroupM confirms layoffs of staffers across N. America, EMEA regions
summary: GroupM, the largest media agency, is conducting layoffs across its global network, impacting 114 to 126 employees in North America and EMEA regions. These cutbacks are attributed to a realignment of roles following mergers within GroupM last April, including the formation of EssenceMediacom and GroupM Nexus. The timing also coincides with an economic downturn and recent client losses, although GroupM states the reductions are part of internal "hygiene" and not as extensive as those seen in Big Tech.

title: When data moves, money moves: Western Union analyzes cloud data technologies
summary: Western Union's global head of engineering and architecture, Harveer Singh, discusses the company's increasing reliance on cloud data technologies to facilitate money movement across the globe. He highlights the shift from on-premises infrastructure to the cloud, primarily utilizing AWS, to enhance efficiency and security while navigating complex regulatory landscapes. The article also touches upon the need for improved cohesion among hyperscale cloud providers and the importance of maintaining owned infrastructures in highly regulated industries.

title: Temu Review: What Is Temu and Why Is It Suddenly America’s Most Popular App?
summary: Temu, the American sister brand of China's Pinduoduo, has rapidly become America's most popular shopping app since its U.S. launch last fall. Its success is primarily attributed to extremely low prices, free shipping, and aggressive advertising. While the author found good deals on certain electronics and kitchen items, he advises caution on other categories and notes the app's business model involves cutting out middlemen for direct sales.

title: U.S. agency says Amazon.com exposed workers to safety hazards
summary: A U.S. government agency has cited Amazon.com Inc. for exposing warehouse workers to safety hazards that led to serious injuries. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) found that Amazon's processes, designed for speed over safety, contributed to musculoskeletal disorders and other risks. Amazon faces over $60,000 in potential fines and states it will appeal the allegations, emphasizing its commitment to worker safety.

title: DAZN and Amazon strike global sports streaming agreement
summary: DAZN Group Ltd has partnered with Amazon.com Inc to distribute its sports streaming service on Prime Video Channels. This agreement allows Prime Video customers to access DAZN's live and on-demand sports content for an additional monthly fee. The rollout began in Spain and Germany and will expand to other markets, including Japan, throughout 2023.

title: Where to now for Alibaba in the post-Jack Ma era?
summary: Jack Ma has relinquished control of Ant Group, signaling the potential end of China's tech crackdown. This shift places Alibaba CEO Daniel Zhang in a crucial position to rebuild trust with the government and navigate the company through domestic challenges like increased competition and a struggling cloud unit by focusing on pragmatic management and international expansion. Alibaba aims to achieve 2 billion global annual active users by 2036, pushing into cross-border e-commerce and local markets while facing competition from rivals and internal struggles.

Although Amazon's stock has recently pulled back, the author believes it still offers significant long-term growth potential, whereas Walmart's future growth hinges critically on the flawless execution of its e-commerce strategy.

title: Lowe's Cos. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Lowe's Companies (LOW) stock experienced a 3.06% decline on Thursday, closing at $202.13. This performance lagged behind the broader market, with both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also seeing losses. The stock has now fallen for three consecutive days and its trading volume surpassed its 50-day average.

title: Amazon ends its charity donation program following other cost-cutting efforts
summary: Amazon is discontinuing its AmazonSmile charity donation program by February 20, 2023, as part of broader cost-cutting measures. Since 2013, the program has donated over $400 million to U.S. charities by giving 0.5% of eligible purchases. While Amazon states the impact was spread too thin, many small charities and shoppers have expressed dismay, noting the program's significant benefit to their operations.

summary: This article offers a survival guide for individuals who have been laid off, acknowledging the increasing prevalence of job cuts across various sectors, including tech giants and financial institutions. summary: As major tech companies like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon announce significant layoffs, this article compares the severance packages offered by these and other tech giants like Meta, Salesforce, and Twitter. The article highlights the differing approaches to severance, health benefits, and stock vesting amidst an uncertain job market for laid-off tech workers.

title: Netflix's ability to churn out hits gives it an edge over rivals
summary: Netflix's continuous production of hit shows is positioning it strongly in the competitive streaming market, leading analysts to predict double-digit revenue growth later this year. Following a strong fourth quarter where it surpassed subscriber addition estimates, Netflix shares surged. The company plans to implement features this quarter to convert password sharers into paying subscribers and grow its ad-supported tier.

title: Amazon, Microsoft Job Cuts Deal Another Blow to Ailing Seattle
summary: Job cuts at Amazon and Microsoft are impacting Seattle, America's second-largest tech hub, which is already struggling to recover from the pandemic's blow to its commuter economy. While the 28,000 global job losses might seem small for the region's 2.1 million workforce, this development is a significant psychological setback, making investors and businesses hesitant about new projects and expansion. This further exacerbates the economic challenges faced by the city.

title: Amazon to Plow Extra $35 Billion Into Virginia Data Centers in Cloud Race
summary: Amazon's cloud unit, Amazon Web Services (AWS), plans to invest an additional $35 billion in new data centers in Virginia by 2040. This move aims to reinforce its leading position against competitors like Microsoft and Alphabet. The expansion is expected to create 1,000 jobs in the state, which is a crucial hub for AWS operations.

summary: General Mills attended the 2023 Consumer Electronics Show (CES) to explore emerging technologies and their impact on consumers' eating habits and the food industry. General Mills plans to translate this inspiration into action by exploring partnerships, such as with Smarter, to enhance kitchen experiences and gather consumer data.

summary: Sonoco Products has activated a 1 MW rooftop solar array at its Dayton, N.J., warehouse, aiming to generate 1.295 million kWh of clean power annually and meet 58% of the facility's electricity needs. This initiative is part of Sonoco's broader sustainability goals, which include reducing Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by at least 25% and energy consumption by 8% across its global manufacturing operations by 2030, aligning with the Science Based Targets framework. summary: This article evaluates the iShares U.S. Consumer Discretionary ETF (IYC) as an investment option. title: Spotify to slash 6% of workforce, adding to tech layoffs glut | Daily Sabah
summary: Spotify announced it will lay off 6% of its 10,000 employees, amounting to about 600 people, as the music streaming giant prepares for a possible recession and aligns costs with revenue growth. CEO Daniel Ek admitted he was "too ambitious in investing ahead of our revenue growth." This move follows similar layoffs across the tech sector, including Google, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft, as companies face economic headwinds and a downturn in demand after pandemic-driven growth.

title: Yankee Candle owner Newell Brands cuts 13% of its workforce, will close Deerfield office
summary: Newell Brands, the owner of Yankee Candle, is implementing a significant corporate restructuring, including a 13% global workforce reduction and the closure of its corporate offices in South Deerfield, Massachusetts, and Boca Raton, Florida. Remaining employees from South Deerfield will relocate to local offices, while Boca Raton staff will work remotely. These changes are expected to save Newell Brands between $220 million and $250 million annually, and the company's manufacturing, distribution, and research facilities, along with the Yankee Candle flagship store, will remain operational.

title: Amazon’s second wave of layoffs hits thousands of employees across three states
summary: Amazon has executed a second round of layoffs, affecting over 3,000 employees across New York, California, and Washington. The job cuts were formally reported to the respective states and are part of a larger mass layoff initiative. The notices indicate effective dates for the layoffs ranging from March to April.

title: Amazon Pharmacy Introduces RxPass: Unlimited Prescription Medications for Only $5 a Month, Delivered Free to your Door—Available Exclusively for Prime Members
summary: Amazon Pharmacy has launched RxPass, a new Prime membership benefit offering unlimited access to common generic medications for $5 a month, with free delivery. This service aims to provide affordable and convenient access to prescriptions for over 80 common health conditions, allowing Prime members to save significantly, especially those taking multiple medications monthly. It complements existing Prime prescription savings and other Amazon Pharmacy services, including options for those with and without insurance.

title: The Best Leggings for Literally Everything
summary: SELF's 2023 Activewear Awards present a curated list of the best leggings for various activities, from intense workouts to everyday lounging. The selection process involved extensive testing by 45 individuals and focused on criteria like waistband fit, fabric quality, and activity-specific features, with a strong emphasis on size inclusivity. The article highlights top picks across categories like compression, lounging, everyday wear, yoga, strength training, and cold weather, including "All-Time Bests" that testers consistently love.

title: Technology & Innovation Highlights from Q4 2022
summary: Lockheed Martin's Q4 2022 highlights include the successful completion of the Orion spacecraft's NASA mission, a significant F-35 procurement contract with Germany, and advancements in hypersonic flight testing. The company also made strides in sustainable energy storage, optionally piloted Black Hawk helicopters, and secured full-rate production for the CH-53K helicopter. Other notable achievements involve new production sites, space communication technology, inflatable habitats, radar contracts, and the delivery of the Mid-Range Capability battery to the U.S. Army.

title: SentinelOne Announces Executive Appointments and Promotions Amidst Rapid Growth
summary: SentinelOne (NYSE: S) has announced key executive appointments and promotions to bolster its cybersecurity platform and scale go-to-market operations. Mitra Mahdavian, Bryan Gale, Rajiv Taori, Eric Tinker, and Joni Tsumas have been appointed to VP or SVP roles, while Jared Phipps and Daniel Kollberg received promotions. These changes aim to enhance the company's ability to deliver advanced XDR protection and innovation to its global customers.

title: Axon Enterprise And A Lesson In 50,000% Gains (NASDAQ:AXON)
summary: This article examines Axon Enterprise, Inc.'s remarkable 50,000% gains over two decades, emphasizing how long-term investing can yield significant returns despite market volatility and challenges. The author discusses applying long-term investment logic to potential multi-baggers and introduces VirTra, a microcap in law enforcement, as a company with similarities to early Axon. The piece also delves into the author's personal investment philosophy, which favors long-term holds and identifying undervalued growth opportunities.

title: Walmart raises minimum wage as retail labor market remains tight
summary: Walmart is increasing its minimum wage for store employees to $14 an hour, part of a move that will raise the company's U.S. average hourly wage to over $17.50. This change impacts about 340,000 workers and comes as other companies face economic headwinds, but the retail labor market remains tight. Walmart is also enhancing its college tuition program and creating more higher-paying roles to attract and retain staff.

title: Walmart to raise minimum wage for U.S. hourly workers to $14
summary: Walmart announced it will raise its average hourly wage for U.S. store workers to $17.50, up from $17, with the minimum wage increasing to a range of $14-$19 per hour depending on location. This move, affecting approximately 340,000 workers across 3,000 stores, aims to attract and retain employees in a competitive labor market, though its new minimum still lags behind some rivals like Amazon and Costco. The decision comes amidst moderating U.S. wage growth but a robust labor market.

title: The Makers of Cadet Brand Launch Line of New, Patent-Pending Bully Chews for Dogs
summary: Cadet, a brand under Central Garden & Pet, has launched a new line of patent-pending Bully Hide chews for dogs. These chews combine a bully stick exterior with a beef hide interior, offering an all-natural, highly palatable, and digestible long-lasting option at an affordable price point. The unique technology aims to provide a wholesome treat for pets and their parents.

title: Choice Hotels Opens Cambria Hotel Austin Uptown Near the Domain
summary: Choice Hotels International has opened the Cambria Hotel Austin Uptown Near the Domain, marking its second property in Austin, Texas, with a third on the way. The 135-room hotel is strategically located in Austin's high-tech corridor, providing convenient access to major tech companies and local attractions. It offers modern amenities and design-forward accommodations aimed at both business and leisure travelers.

title: IMAA welcomes seven new media partners for 2023
summary: The Independent Media Agencies of Australia (IMAA) has announced seven new media partners for 2023, bringing their total to 44. The new partners include Amazon Ads, BrandSpace, Integral Ad Science (IAS), Reddit, Sports Entertainment Network (SEN), StackAdapt, and Taboola. IMAA's chair, Jacquie Alley, highlighted the association's continued growth and the significance of these partnerships for independent agencies in Australia.

title: Big Tech to Congress: Listen to Taylor Swift and Go After Ticketmaster, Not Us
summary: Lobbyists for major technology companies capitalized on public outrage over Ticketmaster's handling of Taylor Swift concert tickets to deflect congressional antitrust scrutiny away from Big Tech. They argued that Congress should focus on clear monopolies like Ticketmaster, implying that existing antitrust laws are sufficient and that efforts to reform them to target tech giants are misguided. This strategy led to a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing focusing on Live Nation/Ticketmaster's monopolistic practices instead of Big Tech.

title: Simply Good Foods expands Quest brand
summary: Simply Good Foods Co. is expanding its Quest brand with the introduction of Quest cheese crackers, available in a "Cheddar Blast" variety. These new crackers offer 10 grams of protein and 5 grams of net carbs per serving, addressing consumer demand for savory snacking options that align with nutrition and wellness goals. This launch follows the recent debut of Quest mini peanut butter cups, further diversifying the brand's product line.

title: Chipotle Plans to Hire 15,000 People Ahead of ‘Burrito Season’
summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill announced plans to hire 15,000 new workers in anticipation of its busiest period, dubbed "burrito season," which runs from March to May. This hiring spree contrasts with other large companies that are implementing layoffs. The company aims to nearly double its North American outlets to 7,000 and needs more staff to support this aggressive growth and manage increased sales during the spring.

title: How Quantum Computing Will Transform Our World
summary: Quantum computing, while still developing, promises to revolutionize various fields by processing information at an exponentially faster rate than traditional computers. Companies like IBM are leading the charge, developing advanced quantum processors and exploring applications in areas like finance, materials science, and AI. However, this transformative technology also presents significant national security risks, particularly concerning the obsolescence of current cryptography, prompting a global race to develop quantum-safe security measures.

title: Intel shares drop on weak quarterly results and expectations for another quarter of losses
summary: Intel's shares fell after the company reported weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter results and provided a soft forecast for the first quarter of 2023. The chipmaker experienced a significant decline in revenue for the fourth consecutive quarter due to a downturn in PC chip sales and broader economic headwinds. The company also announced a net loss for Q4 and anticipates further losses in Q1, leading to concerns about its financial performance in the near future.

title: Lowe's Cos. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Lowe's Cos. (LOW) stock fell 2.09% on Thursday, closing at $201.81, despite a positive trading session for the broader market with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both rising. The stock underperformed competitors like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) but fared better than Home Depot Inc. (HD) and Walmart Inc. (WMT), which also saw slight declines. This marked the second consecutive day of losses for Lowe's, with its trading volume exceeding its 50-day average.

title: IBM Is Tech’s Most Beaten-Down Company
summary: This article argues that IBM has significantly fallen from its former prominence, ranking 49th on the Fortune 500 compared to 8th in 1980. Its recent financial results show flat revenue and modest net income, trailing far behind other tech giants like Apple, Amazon, and Microsoft. The author criticizes IBM for missing key technological advancements such as cloud computing, search, e-commerce, and operating systems despite its past R&D capabilities.

title: Dow Chemical to cut 2,000 jobs
summary: Dow Chemical announced Thursday it will cut approximately 2,000 jobs from its workforce as part of a plan to achieve $1 billion in cost savings in 2023. The company has been battling soaring energy costs following the Russian invasion of Ukraine and reported a 17% drop in net sales during the fourth quarter of 2022. This move aligns with a trend of major corporations, particularly in the tech industry, implementing mass layoffs recently.

title: Licking County becomes the 'bullseye' for development one year after Intel
summary: One year after Intel announced its plans for a $20 billion computer chip manufacturing facility in Licking County, Ohio, the area has become a hub for development. This growth has led to escalating property values and changes in the rural landscape, causing some residents to relocate. While the Intel project promises significant economic benefits and job creation, local officials are also grappling with challenges like funding disparities and utility expansion conflicts.

title: News | Amazon Lands Buyer for Bay Area Office Campus Amid Company’s Real Estate Contraction
summary: Amazon is selling its four-building Metro Corporate Center office campus in Milpitas, California, to Dermody Properties for conversion into warehouse space. This disposition is part of Amazon's larger real estate contraction and efforts to cut rising expenses following a period of rapid pandemic-era expansion. The company originally purchased the property for $123 million in late 2021 and is also undergoing significant job cuts.

title: Walmart Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Walmart Inc. (WMT) stock saw a 0.77% increase to $143.30 on Friday, outperforming the broader market during a favorable trading session. The company's stock closed below its 52-week high but ended a two-day losing streak. However, it underperformed against some competitors like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN).

title: Rockford airport pursuing 4 new travel destinations to boost passenger numbers
summary: The Chicago Rockford International Airport (RFD) saw an 18% increase in passenger traffic in 2022, nearly reaching pre-pandemic levels. Airport officials are now exploring four new travel destinations, including Denver, Dallas, Nashville, Austin, Texas, and Asheville, North Carolina, based on passenger feedback and market leakage from the Chicago area. They are in discussions with Allegiant Air and other commercial airlines to expand service, emphasizing the strong local demand for air travel.

title: Here's Why Pizza Boxes Are Still Getting Slammed
summary: Pizza boxes have presented a significant engineering challenge since the first delivery boxes appeared in the 1940s. Despite improvements like corrugated cardboard in the 1960s and the "pizza saver," issues like steam-induced sogginess and "rubbery grossness" in cheese persist. Ambitious attempts, such as Zume Inc.'s Pizza Pod, have offered innovative solutions but faced challenges in manufacturing and cost, leaving the pizza box problem largely unresolved.

title: Google continued to ramp up federal lobbying spending before DOJ filed second antitrust lawsuit
summary: Google's parent company, Alphabet, significantly increased its federal lobbying expenditures, spending over $13 million in 2022, prior to the Department of Justice filing its second antitrust lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges Google monopolized the digital advertising technology sector by acquiring rivals and manipulating the auction process to stifle competition. Despite these lobbying efforts and substantial political contributions, particularly to Democratic candidates, Alphabet also announced mass layoffs of 12,000 employees in January 2023.

title: S3 Intelligent-Tiering's Archive Instant Access Tier
summary: Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering now includes an Archive Instant Access (AIA) tier, which automatically moves infrequently accessed data to a more cost-effective storage class while still allowing sub-millisecond retrieval. This tier offers benefits such as no retrieval charges, no minimum storage duration, and zero operational overhead, making it ideal for data with unpredictable access patterns, backups, and log files. NetApp BlueXP Cloud Volumes ONTAP can further extend these benefits by enabling automatic tiering between EBS and S3 Intelligent-Tiering, along with other data management features.

title: After A Slow Start, TikTok Doubles Down On Ambition to Dominate Social Commerce
summary: TikTok, despite privacy concerns, is aggressively pursuing dominance in social commerce, leveraging its engaging video content, cheap ads, and influencer market. While its "TikTok Shop" had a slow start in Western markets compared to Asia, the platform is expanding and seeing increased engagement for in-app purchases. TikTok's advertising strategy, offering lower costs and effective audience targeting, positions it for significant growth in ad revenue, despite being years behind rivals in some areas, and is already influencing consumer purchasing habits.

title: Internet Records Historic $1 Trillion Consumer Milestone
summary: Comscore announced that the internet surpassed $1 trillion in U.S. online retail consumer spending in 2022, marking a 21% year-over-year increase. Mobile devices played a crucial role, accounting for almost 40% of the total digital commerce and growing faster than desktop spending. This milestone highlights the accelerated adoption of online purchasing, with significant growth in categories like event tickets, digital content, and apparel.

title: W3BCLOUD SPAC: Everything you need to know about W3BCLOUD stock
summary: W3BCLOUD, a technology company focused on providing infrastructure for web3 technologies, plans to go public via a SPAC merger with Social Leverage Acquisition Corp I. Despite a "crypto winter" leading to 95% of shares being redeemed by investors and several other crypto companies cancelling SPAC plans, W3BCLOUD is seeking an extension to raise the necessary $150 million for the merger. The company, a joint venture between AMD and ConsenSys, builds and manages decentralized data centers and was most recently valued at $1.25 billion (though this has been adjusted due to redemptions) and aims to expand its global network to support the growing web3 ecosystem.

title: With a GOL plane, AerCap celebrates the delivery of its 50th Boeing 737-800 converted to a freighter
summary: AerCap Holdings NV announced the delivery of its 50th Boeing 737-800 Converted Freighter (BCF), which was converted at COOPESA and delivered to GOL Linhas Aéreas for operation on behalf of Mercado Livre. AerCap Cargo was the launch customer for the 737-800BCF program in 2016 and has seen unprecedented demand for express air cargo. This milestone highlights the versatility and reliability of the 737-800BCF as a sought-after narrow-body freighter.

title: Amgen lays off 300, does not disclose whether any are in Thousand Oaks
summary: Amgen, a Thousand Oaks-based biotech company, announced workforce restructuring resulting in approximately 300 layoffs, about 1.3% of its global workforce. The company stated the job cuts are mainly in the commercial team in the United States, but did not specify if any were in its Thousand Oaks headquarters. This follows other major tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and Amazon also announcing significant layoffs, and Amgen released Q4 2022 financial results showing flat revenue and a 15% decrease in net income compared to the previous year.

title: Amazon’s holiday sales growth outpaced superstore competitors in 2022
summary: Amazon's U.S. consumer sales during the 2022 holiday season grew by 9 percent year-over-year, surpassing its performance in the previous three years. This growth rate outpaced several major superstore competitors like Target and Costco, matching only Walmart. Other retailers such as Best Buy and Bed Bath & Beyond experienced declines in holiday sales.

title: NetApp, a specialist in cloud data management, says it will lay off 8%, or around 960 people, citing economic climate
summary: NetApp, a cloud data management company, announced it will lay off 8% of its global workforce, approximately 960 employees, due to "macroeconomic challenges and the reduced spending environment." The company anticipates a charge of $85 million to $95 million related to these cuts, which will take place across multiple geographies. This move is part of a broader trend of significant layoffs within the tech sector this year.

title: Top Performing Leveraged/Inverse ETFs: 01/29/2023
summary: This article highlights the top-performing leveraged and inverse ETFs for the week ending January 29, 2023. Key drivers for these strong performances include positive Tesla earnings, growth in electric and autonomous vehicles, and hopes for a slower pace of interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, boosting technology and consumer discretionary sectors. The list provides specific ETF tickers, their names, and weekly returns, along with brief explanations for their performance.
